art.subject: Daurian Jackdaw (Corvus dauuricus), pied adult in winter (October–March): forehead, crown, face and nape black with a purple gloss; silvery greyish-white streaks on the feathers behind the eye and over the rear ear-coverts; chin and throat black glossed blue; a broad creamy greyish-white collar wraps round the neck and joins the greyish-white breast and belly; back, wings and tail glossy black; underwing coverts, axillaries and undertail coverts slate-black; short stubby black bill; dark grey-brown iris; black legs and feet.
art.pose: perched in a bare tree among a large flock
art.scene: Korean winter lowland fields and forest edge with bare trees; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched: purple-glossed black crown and face, silvery-grey streaks behind the eye, glossy black throat, broad greyish-white collar running into greyish-white underparts, glossy black back, wings and tail, black legs
adult, in flight seen from below: greyish-white collar, breast and belly contrasting with the black head, throat, underwings and undertail coverts; square black tail; head, body and tail in line
first-winter, side view perched: almost entirely sooty black with little gloss, silvery-grey streaks on the rear ear-coverts, dark eye, short stubby black bill
art.build: Small, compact crow, 33cm — about the length of a feral pigeon and far smaller than a Carrion Crow, with a round head, steep forehead and short neck. Bill black, short and stubby, about half the length of the head, straight with a gently curved culmen. Legs black, medium length; walks briskly over fields. At rest the wingtips reach close to the tail tip. Tail medium-length and square-ended. Flies with quick, pigeon-like wingbeats, often in flocks mixed with Rooks; from below in flight the pale collar and belly contrast with the black head, underwings and vent.
avoid: Do not paint a pale whitish iris — that is Western Jackdaw (Corvus monedula); the Daurian Jackdaw has a dark eye.
Do not make the adult's underparts dark grey; the collar, breast and belly are a clean, contrasting greyish-white.
Do not paint a long, heavy crow bill or a crow-sized body; the bill is short and stubby and the bird pigeon-sized.
Do not paint a bare whitish face at the bill base (adult Rook, Corvus frugilegus).
